questions.scenario: A company has database servers that will run at the same size, in the same region, 24/7 for the next three years.
questions.question: Which pricing option will most likely give the biggest predictable saving?

options.why: No discount; best for variable workloads.
Correct. Stable, long-running resources benefit most from reservations.
Spot VMs can be evicted, which is unsuitable for databases.
Free allowances do not cover production database servers.

questions.explanation: Reservations trade a 1- or 3-year commitment for large discounts on predictable workloads.

questions.question: Which Azure pricing option uses unused capacity at a deep discount, but the VM can be evicted when Azure needs the capacity back?

options.why: Hybrid Benefit is a licensing benefit.
Dedicated Hosts are physical servers for one customer.

questions.explanation: Spot VMs offer large discounts on spare capacity with eviction risk.

questions.question: A company already owns Windows Server licences with Software Assurance. Which option can reduce the cost of running Windows VMs in Azure?

options.why: Correct. It lets you apply eligible existing licences.
Advisor recommends optimisations but is not a licensing benefit.
Policy enforces rules; it does not change prices.

questions.explanation: Azure Hybrid Benefit lets you reuse eligible Windows Server and SQL Server licences.

questions.question: Which TWO pricing options require a one- or three-year commitment?

options.why: No commitment; capacity can be evicted.

questions.explanation: Reservations and savings plans both use 1- or 3-year commitments in exchange for discounts.
